title: When Qualitron Failed, Stan Shih Started Multitech on NT$1 Million
conflicts: Founding date (Acer: 1 August 1976; CHM and IT History: September 1976) handled as 'second half of 1976'. Number of partners varies (four including Yeh; Yeh and three; Yeh and five), so no count is given. HQ city (Hsinchu per IT History/HomeComputerMuseum vs Taipei per the slate and Shih's 1996 remark) not asserted. Renaming year (1981/1987/1989) avoided. 3,000-engineer training figure is Acer's own and attributed to Acer.
notes: Shih's memoir is quoted via the Calcuseum Qualitron page (the book itself is not online). Episode framed as a founding born of necessity after Qualitron's collapse, with the ownership-sharing and teaching decisions; the slate's 'teaching microprocessors in Taipei' is kept as the Microprocessor Training Centre (1978) without a city.
